chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Abbas, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Imam settles the debts of the believers, except for the dowries of the women.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam, referring to the religious and political leader in Shia theology
key_terms.مُهُورَ: Dowries or bridal gifts (plural of mahr)

ai.seo_question: What debts does the Imam pay for believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the scope of the Imam’s financial intercession, establishing that while he settles general debts to ensure the believer's honor and creditworthiness, he excludes dowries (mehar) as they are considered a private contractual right of the wife. This distinction highlights the Shia legal principle that the Imam’s guarantee covers public or communal obligations but respects specific private liabilities, reinforcing the concept of the Imam as the ultimate guarantor of the community's social and economic stability.
